newsitem.title: USA: Houston Ship Channel one-way restrictions remain.
newsitem.headline: Houston Ship Channel one-way restrictions remain.

text.p: Deep-draft shipping traffic remained restricted to one-way at a time on Monday along a section of the Houston Ship Channel where a barge lost a load of six large tanks last week, officials said.

Draft restrictions were lifted on Sunday between milepost 52 and milepost 56 on the channel, where the tanks fell overboard last Thursday after the barge they were on was swept by the wake of a passing ship.
"We're still moving ships one-way only, but there's nobody waiting right now," a dispatcher with the Houston Ship Channel Pilots' Association said.
A U.S. Army Corps of Engineers side-sweep sonar ship has found all six of the tanks and salvage operations were expected to begin today, a U.S. Coast Guard spokesman said.

The sonar ship over the weekend determined that none of the tanks appeared to be blocking the channel, and shipping returned to near-normal along the waterway linking the Port of Houston and refinery row to the Gulf of Mexico.
